question: The S&P 500 fell 57% from October 2007 to March 2009. By what percentage did it then have to rise to recover?
answer: About 133%: a fall of 57% leaves 43%, which must more than double. It took until 2013.
move: Losses and gains work on different bases, so losses cost more to undo.
ask: Which loss am I expecting an equal-sized gain to repair?
trap: 57%, as if a rise undid an equal fall.
hint: Start from £100, take the fall, then ask what multiplies the rest back to £100.
steps: A rise of about 133%, more than double the fall.
source: S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P 500 closing values, 2007 to 2013
reference: S&P Dow Jones Indices, S&P 500 closing values: 1,565.15 on 9 October 2007 and 676.53 on 9 March 2009
